memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient is a 57‑year‑old male shop owner from Vijayanagar, Bengaluru. He reports increased thirst, occasional fatigue, no weight loss. Random capillary glucose 162 mg/dL. BMI 27.4 kg/m2, blood pressure 128/82 mmHg, lungs clear. No retinopathy signs on basic eye check. HbA1c not yet done. Assessment: newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, asymptomatic hyperglycemia. Plan: start metformin 500 mg BD, glimepiride 1 mg OD before breakfast, sitagliptin 100 mg OD, empagliflozin 10 mg OD. Review in 6 weeks with labs and spirometry (baseline).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Metformin 500 mg tablet – take one tablet twice daily.
Glimepiride 1 mg tablet – take one tablet each morning before breakfast.
Sitagliptin 100 mg tablet – take one tablet daily.
Empagliflozin 10 mg tablet – take one tablet daily.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Allergy: Sulfonamide – rash and pruritus after taking co-trimoxazole for urinary tract infection 2 years ago. Avoid sulfonamide antibiotics.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
HbA1c: 7.8% (ref 4.0‑5.6%).
Fasting plasma glucose: 155 mg/dL (ref 70‑99).
Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio: 32 mg/g (ref <30).
Serum creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (ref 0.6‑1.2).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Dilated fundus exam: mild non‑proliferative diabetic retinopathy, microaneurysms temporal to macula, no macular edema. Visual acuity 6/6 both eyes. Recommend annual retinal screening.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus – review.
Patient reports improved thirst, occasional mild hypoglycemia symptoms before lunch. Finger‑stick glucose 78‑92 mg/dL fasting, post‑prandial 140‑155. Spirometry: FEV1 2.85 L (92% predicted), FVC 3.40 L (88%), FEV1/FVC 0.84; change from baseline +0.05 L. ACT score 22 (well controlled). Inhaler technique not applicable. Smoking status: never. Plan: increase metformin to 850 mg BD for better glycaemic control, keep other meds. Review in 8 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Metformin 850 mg tablet – take one tablet twice daily.
Glimepiride 1 mg tablet – take one tablet each morning before breakfast.
Sitagliptin 100 mg tablet – take one tablet daily.
Empagliflozin 10 mg tablet – take one tablet daily.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been feeling a tingling sensation in both feet, especially at night. It’s mild but worries me. Should I be concerned about diabetic neuropathy?

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with possible peripheral neuropathy.
Patient describes bilateral foot tingling, worse at night, no weakness. Sensory exam: decreased light touch sensation to distal great toes, proprioception intact. No foot ulcers. Plan: check vitamin B12, start neuropathic pain agent if needed. Refer to neurology for further evaluation. Continue current diabetes meds.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to Neurology, Dr. K. Rao, for evaluation of peripheral neuropathy in a 57‑year‑old male with type 2 diabetes. Symptoms: bilateral foot tingling, nocturnal, mild. Request nerve conduction studies and advice on symptomatic treatment.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Neurology report: Nerve conduction shows mild sensory axonal neuropathy, motor nerves normal. No compressive etiology. Recommend pregabalin 75 mg BD for neuropathic pain, foot care education, glycemic control. Follow‑up in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Pregabalin 75 mg capsule – take one capsule twice daily after food.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
HbA1c: 7.2% (ref 4.0‑5.6%).
Fasting plasma glucose: 130 mg/dL (ref 70‑99).
Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio: 28 mg/g (ref <30).
Serum creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (ref 0.6‑1.2).

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for diabetes review with Dr Suresh Menon (D05) on 2026-04-15 at 10:30 AM. Please bring glucose log and foot inspection notes.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus – follow‑up.
Patient reports foot tingling improved after pregabalin, occasional mild numbness. No hypoglycemia episodes. Labs: HbA1c 7.0% (target <7.5), FPG 118 mg/dL, urine ACR 26 mg/g. Spirometry: FEV1 2.90 L (94% predicted), FVC 3.45 L (90%), FEV1/FVC 0.84; change +0.05 L since last. ACT score 23 (well controlled). Inhaler technique N/A. Smoking: never. Plan: discontinue glimepiride due to risk of hypoglycemia, continue metformin 850 mg BD, sitagliptin 100 mg OD, empagliflozin 10 mg OD, pregabalin 75 mg BD. Review in 4 months.
